Legionary base under a living town; tests continuity of occupation against naming.
The northern limes command; the terminus of the road through Napoca.
Seat of the gold administration; an administrative rather than military centre.

Constantine's bridgehead; a crossing that outlived the province.

Greek foundation on the littoral; silted out of use and out of the charts.

Nösen and Bistritz over a Slavic hydronym.
A Saxon seat with a compact and well-dated charter record.

Wallachian princely seat with a dense internal charter record.
Late to the maps and central to them afterwards; the seam Trench E excavates.
The first Wallachian seat; textual evidence far outruns cartographic.
Langenau and Dlugopole beside the Romanian name.
The Oltenian centre; covered by the Habsburg occupation survey of 1718–39.
Moldavian princely seat named in Cantemir and in the charters before him.
